mainTopic: יום טוב laws of wicks, preparing ovens and pots, and building-like acts, along with רב נתן בר אבא's teachings on compassion and dependence
overview: The גמרא finishes its discussion of wicks on יום טוב. Cutting a wick by fire is allowed only between two lamps. One may remove the burnt part of a wick (מוחטין). בר קפרא lists three strict and three lenient wick laws. Next come several teachings of רב נתן בר אבא: the rich of בבל lacked compassion, as the story of שבתאי בר מרינוס shows, and whoever depends on others' tables lives a dark life, which a ברייתא supports. A new משנה then forbids several cooking preparations on יום טוב: breaking earthenware, sweeping an oven, setting up barrels for a pot, propping a pot, and leading an animal with a stick. The גמרא explains that breaking earthenware counts as מתקן מנא. It allows sweeping an oven when baking is impossible otherwise, and it permits plastering an oven with ready riverbank mud or with ashes. Finally, it separates בנין קבע from בנין עראי, allows bathroom stones out of human dignity, and rules that a bonfire may be stacked from the top down but not from the bottom up.

steps.title: If cutting a wick fixes a vessel, so does cutting it by fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason for banning cutting a wick in two: cutting it with fire also makes a usable item.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the reason is that he is fixing a vessel, then cutting it in the fire is also fixing a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing the reason why the משנה forbids cutting a wick into two on יום טוב. It points out that the same reason should also forbid cutting it with fire, which רבי יהודה allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the problem is מתקן מנא, making a new usable item out of one long wick. Then cutting with fire also produces two usable wicks. So why would fire be allowed while a knife is not?

keyTerms.meaning: Fixing or completing a vessel; making an item ready for use, which is forbidden

phrases.english: [If it is] because he is fixing a vessel,
phrases.notes: This continues the question 'What is the reason?' on the previous amud.

phrases.english: with fire he is also fixing a vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proposed reason for the משנה's ban on cutting a wick in two
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason of מתקן מנא for forbidding cutting a wick
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fire-cutting also produces two usable wicks, so the reason should forbid it too. Yet it is allowed.

steps.title: Cutting by fire happens only between two lamps
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that fire-cutting is permitted only when the wick sits in two lamps and is cut by lighting them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: He cuts it with fire at the mouths of two lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers the challenge by showing exactly how the permitted fire-cutting works. The wick is stretched between two lamps and burned in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not simply cut a wick to make two wicks. He lights a long wick that runs between two lamps, and the split happens on its own as part of lighting them. Since the wick is used right away for light, it is not seen as making a new item.

keyTerms.meaning: At the mouths of two lamps

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:
He cuts it with fire at the mouths of two lamps.
phrases.notes: The cutting happens while lighting two lamps at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the permitted case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: the permitted fire-cutting only happens during lighting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any cutting with fire is allowed, even though it makes two wicks
steps.terutzMaskana: Fire-cutting is allowed only between two lamps, where the split comes from lighting

steps.title: רב permits מוחטין of a wick on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אבא quotes רב that one may do מוחטין to a wick on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אבא said in the name of רב: One may do מוחטין to the wick on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about wicks is brought in: a certain action called מוחטין is allowed on יום טוב. The word is unclear, so this step sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself is a heter. However, the key word is unfamiliar, so the גמרא will need to define it before we know what is actually permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An unclear word for treating a wick; it is defined in the next steps

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Abba said that Rav said:
One may 'mochet' the wick on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on the same topic of wicks
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוחטין of a wick is permitted on יום טוב

steps.title: What does מוחטין mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word מוחטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is מוחטין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about what the word means. This is not an attack on רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot apply רב's ruling without knowing which action it allows. The question only asks for a definition.

phrases.english: What is 'mochatin'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in רב's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מוחטין

steps.title: מוחטין means removing the darkened part
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא בר שלמיא explains that it means removing the burnt, dark part of the wick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: To remove the darkness.
steps.whatsHappening: The word is defined: it means removing the charred tip of a wick so the lamp burns brighter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burnt charcoal on a wick dims the light. Removing it is allowed on יום טוב because it improves the light, and the person is not making a new item.

keyTerms.meaning: Darkness; here, the burnt, blackened part

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא (מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב):
phrases.english: Rav Chanina bar Shelemya said (in the name of Rav):
To remove the darkness [the charred part].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוחטין means removing the burnt, dark part of the wick

steps.title: Six wick laws: three strict and three lenient
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא lists six יום טוב laws about wicks: three prohibitions and three permissions.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: Six things were said about a wick, three strict and three lenient. Strict: one may not twist it from scratch on יום טוב, one may not singe it in fire, and one may not cut it in two. Lenient: one may crush it by hand, soak it in oil, and cut it with fire at the mouths of two lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא sums up the whole topic in a neat list of six wick laws. It also repeats רבי חייא's rule about cutting between two lamps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a wick from scratch, singeing it, and cutting it in two are forbidden. Each of these prepares a new usable item. Crushing it by hand and soaking it in oil are minor adjustments, so they are allowed. Cutting by fire is allowed only between two lamps, as part of lighting.
steps.whatToRemember: Forbidden on יום טוב: twisting a new wick, singeing it, or cutting it in two. Permitted: crushing it by hand, soaking it in oil, or cutting it with fire between two lamps.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
Six things were said regarding a wick.
Three to be strict, and three to be lenient.

phrases.aramaic: לְהַחְמִיר: אֵין גּוֹדְלִין אוֹתָהּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: To be strict: one may not twist it from the start on a Festival,
and one may not singe it in fire,
and one may not cut it in two.
To be lenient: one may crush it by hand,
and soak it in oil,
and cut it with fire at the mouths of two lamps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the wick laws and confirms רבי חייא's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three wick actions are forbidden on יום טוב and three are permitted

steps.title: The rich people of בבל are headed to גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אבא quotes רב that the wealthy people of בבל will go down to גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נתן בר אבא said in the name of רב: The wealthy of בבל are those who go down to גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now leaves the topic of wicks. It quotes another teaching from the same רב נתן בר אבא, this time a harsh statement about the rich of בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching is placed here only because it has the same speaker as the wick ruling. Its subject has nothing to do with wicks. The reason for this harsh judgment comes in the story that follows.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a link to the wick laws. The only connection is that the same speaker, רב נתן בר אבא, said both teachings.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Natan bar Abba said that Rav said:
The wealthy of Babylonia are those who descend to Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, linked only by having the same speaker
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wealthy of בבל will go to גיהנם

steps.title: The story of שבתאי בר מרינוס
steps.stepSummary: שבתאי בר מרינוס came to בבל and asked for a business partnership and then for food, and the rich refused both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this case: שבתאי בר מרינוס came to בבל. He asked them for a business partnership, and they did not give it to him. He asked them to feed him, and they did not feed him either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show why the rich of בבל deserve such a harsh judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he asked for an עיסקא, a business deal in which they would fund him and share the profits. They refused, even though it carried no great loss for them. Then he asked only for basic food, and they refused that too, which shows they had no compassion at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A business partnership with shared profit

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּשַׁבְּתַאי בַּר מָרִינוּס אִקְּלַע לְבָבֶל,
phrases.english: Like this case: Shabbetai bar Marinus happened to come to Babylonia,

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִנַּיְיהוּ עִסְקָא — וְלָא יְהַבוּ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: he asked them for a business partnership, and they did not give him.
[He asked] to be fed food; they also did not feed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the harsh statement with a real event
steps.raayaObject: That the rich of בבל lacked compassion
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of שבתאי בר מרינוס, who was refused both a partnership and food

steps.title: People without compassion are not from אברהם's descendants
steps.stepSummary: שבתאי concluded that these people come from the ערב רב, since compassion is the sign of being from the descendants of אברהם אבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: These people come from the ערב רב, as it says, 'And He will give you compassion and have compassion on you.' Anyone who has compassion on people is surely from the descendants of אברהם אבינו. Anyone who has no compassion on people is surely not from the descendants of אברהם אבינו.
steps.whatsHappening: שבתאי explains what their behavior shows: people this cruel must come from the ערב רב, not from אברהם. This ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links ה׳'s gift of compassion to the promise to the forefathers. This shows that compassion is a basic trait of אברהם's descendants. So a person who acts without any mercy shows by his actions that he does not belong to that family.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixed multitude that left Egypt along with the Jews

steps.whatToRemember: Compassion for others is the sign of being a true descendant of אברהם אבינו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic teaching about Jewish identity: חסד and רחמים are treated as part of who a Jew is, not only as a good extra.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: הָנֵי מֵעֵרֶב רַב קָא אָתוּ,
phrases.english: He said: These people come from the mixed multitude,
as it is written: 'And He will give you compassion and have compassion on you,'
Anyone who has compassion on people,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
phrases.english: it is known that he is from the descendants of Abraham our father,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת —
phrases.english: and anyone who does not have compassion on people,

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ.
phrases.english: it is known that he is not from the descendants of Abraham our father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: הָנֵי מֵעֵרֶב רַב קָא אָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the story, based on a פסוק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Lacking compassion shows that a person is not a true descendant of אברהם אבינו. This explains the harsh judgment on the rich of בבל.

steps.title: Depending on another's table makes the world dark
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אבא quotes רב: whoever depends on other people's tables for food sees the world as dark. He proves this from a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אבא also said in the name of רב: Anyone who looks to other people's tables for food sees the world as dark. The verse says: 'He wanders for bread, asking where it is. He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same speakers as before (רב נתן בר אבא quoting רב). This one is about how bleak life feels when you depend on others for food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of the story of שבתאי בר מרינוס, who was refused food. The verse describes a man wandering for bread who feels that darkness is always close at hand. רב uses it to show that such a person's whole world feels dark.

keyTerms.meaning: one who looks to, waits on, or depends on
the table of others (depending on others for food)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Natan bar Abba said that Rav said:
Whoever looks to the table of others
the world is dark for him,
as it is stated: 'He wanders for bread: Where is it?'

phrases.aramaic: יָדַע כִּי נָכוֹן בְּיָדוֹ יוֹם חֹשֶׁךְ״.
phrases.english: 'He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching of רב נתן בר אבא in the name of רב. It is grouped here mainly because it has the same speakers, though it also touches on the theme of depending on others for food from the story of שבתאי בר מרינוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who depends on others for food experiences the world as dark.

steps.title: Even his life is not a life
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא goes further: such a person's life is not truly a life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Even his life is not a life.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a stronger statement about the person who depends on others' tables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said only that the world feels dark to this person. רב חסדא says that his whole life lacks real living, because he gets no satisfaction from it.

keyTerms.meaning: his life is not a life

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Even his life is not a life.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: אַף חַיָּיו אֵינָן חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב's statement and makes it stronger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who depends on others' tables does not have a real life.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists those whose lives are not lives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three people whose lives are not lives. One of them is the person who depends on his friend's table, which supports רב חסדא. Some add a fourth: a man with only one robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There are three whose lives are not lives. They are: one who looks to his friend's table, one whose wife rules over him, and one whose body is ruled by suffering. And some say: also one who has only one robe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that backs up רב חסדא's words. It also shows a disagreement about whether to add a fourth person to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the exact phrase 'their lives are not lives.' It names the man who depends on his friend's table first, so it supports רב חסדא. The יש אומרים add a man with only one garment, since he cannot wash it and suffers from lice and dirt.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three whose lives are not lives,
and they are: one who looks to the table of his fellow,
and one whose wife rules over him,
and one whose body is ruled by suffering.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד.
phrases.english: And some say: Even one who has only one robe.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה חַיֵּיהֶן אֵינָם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for רב חסדא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that one who depends on others' tables has no real life
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing three whose lives are not lives, starting with one who looks to his friend's table

steps.title: Why the first תנא left out the man with one robe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא did not list the man with one robe because he can check his clothes and remove the lice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא? He holds that it is possible for him to examine his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the תנא קמא, who did not count the man with only one robe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man with one robe can inspect his garment and pick out the lice. His suffering can be relieved, so his life still counts as a life. The other three people have no such easy fix.

keyTerms.meaning: the first Tanna (the opening, unnamed opinion)

phrases.english: And the first Tanna?
It is possible for him to examine his clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the disagreement inside the ברייתא from the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning of an opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a man with one robe also suffers enough to belong on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: He can check and clean his garment, so his suffering is not constant.
steps.whatToRemember: The אגדה ends here: depending on others' tables is counted among the lives that are 'not lives.'

steps.title: No breaking earthenware or cutting paper to roast fish
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that on יום טוב one may not break earthenware or cut paper to roast salted fish on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not break earthenware, and one may not cut paper, in order to roast salted fish on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now opens a new משנה about preparing tools for cooking on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People placed wet shards or paper under salted fish so the fish would not burn. Breaking or cutting them to the right shape is like making a new utensil, so it is forbidden even for cooking on יום טוב.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not break earthenware,
and one may not cut paper
to roast salted fish on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah behind and opens a new משנה on יום טוב laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not break earthenware or cut paper to make a roasting surface for salted fish.
steps.confusionAlert: Roasting the fish is itself allowed on יום טוב. What is forbidden is shaping the shard or paper into a tool.

steps.title: No sweeping out an oven, but pressing down is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: one may not sweep out an oven or stove, but one may press down the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not sweep out an oven or a stove, but one may press down.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule, about getting an oven or stove ready for cooking on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweeping out things that fell into the oven, such as plaster, is forbidden. Flattening the ashes at the bottom so the oven works properly is a lighter act and is permitted. The גמרא later adds an exception to the ban on sweeping (step 20).

phrases.english: And one may not sweep out an oven or stove,
but one may press down.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין גּוֹרְפִין תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם, אֲבָל מְכַבְּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweeping out an oven or stove is forbidden on יום טוב, but pressing down the ashes is permitted.

steps.title: No arranging barrels or propping a pot or door
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: on יום טוב one may not set up two barrels as a makeshift stove, and one may not prop up a pot or a door with a piece of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not set two barrels next to each other to rest a pot on them. And one may not prop up a pot with a piece of wood, and the same applies to a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing things you may not do on יום טוב while preparing food. It adds arranging barrels to hold a pot, and propping a pot or door with wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these acts looks like putting together a structure, which resembles בנין (building). So even though they help with cooking, the משנה forbids them on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: place next to each other, arrange together
to set a pot on the fire or on a support
a piece of wood, a log

phrases.english: And one may not place two barrels next to each other
to set the pot on them,
phrases.notes: The fire would be lit between the barrels, like a makeshift stove.

phrases.english: and one may not prop up the pot with a piece of wood,
and likewise with a door.
phrases.notes: A door may not be propped with wood either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of forbidden cooking preparations in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not arrange barrels to hold a pot, and one may not prop a pot or a door with wood.

steps.title: Leading an animal with a stick
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids leading an animal with a stick on יום טוב, but רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not lead an animal with a stick on יום טוב. רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a new case, driving an animal with a stick. Here there is a disagreement between the first opinion and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (the תנא קמא) forbids it. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows it. The reasons are not given here; the גמרא discusses this case later.

phrases.english: And one may not lead the animal
with a stick on a Festival,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last clause of the משנה, which adds a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids leading an animal with a stick on יום טוב. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: Why is breaking earthenware forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking for the reason behind the משנה's first ruling, not breaking earthenware or cutting paper.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens and asks why the משנה forbade breaking earthenware to roast fish on it. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking a clay shard does not look like a standard forbidden מלאכה. So the גמרא wants to know exactly what the problem is.
steps.confusionAlert: This question goes back to the FIRST ruling of the משנה (step 14, breaking earthenware and cutting paper). It is not about the animal and stick that were just mentioned.

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is finished. The גמרא returns to explain its first clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason it is forbidden to break earthenware or cut paper for roasting fish on יום טוב.

steps.title: Because it prepares a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that breaking the shard or cutting the paper makes a new usable utensil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he is preparing a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: shaping the shard or paper turns it into a usable tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a utensil usable falls under מתקן מנא (fixing or preparing a vessel), which is forbidden on יום טוב. The food benefits from it, but the act itself is making a utensil, not doing the cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: preparing or fixing a utensil for use

phrases.english: Because he is preparing a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Breaking earthenware or cutting paper is forbidden because it counts as preparing a utensil (מתקן מנא).

steps.title: Sweeping is allowed if baking is impossible otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule against sweeping an oven. Then a ברייתא taught by רב חייא בר יוסף adds that if you cannot bake without sweeping, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may not sweep out an oven or stove. רב חייא בר יוסף taught before רב נחמן: if it is impossible to bake unless one sweeps it, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, the ban on sweeping an oven. It brings a teaching that limits that ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ban covers sweeping that is not really needed. When the oven cannot be used at all without sweeping, sweeping becomes part of preparing food (אוכל נפש) and is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a stove with two cooking spots

phrases.english: And one may not sweep out an oven or stove.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Yosef taught before Rav Nachman:
And if it is impossible to bake
unless one sweeps it out, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה and adds a limitation to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweeping an oven on יום טוב is permitted when baking is impossible without it.

steps.title: רבי חייא's wife and the fallen brick
steps.stepSummary: A piece of brick fell into the oven of רבי חייא's wife on יום טוב. He told her he wanted good bread, which hinted that she could remove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A piece of brick fell into the oven of רבי חייא's wife on יום טוב. רבי חייא said to her: See, I want high-quality bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the leniency of step 20 being used in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא did not say directly 'remove the brick.' Instead he said he wanted good bread. Good bread was impossible with the brick inside, so removing it became 'impossible to bake otherwise' and was permitted.

phrases.english: The wife of Rabbi Chiya:

phrases.aramaic: נְפַל לַהּ אֲרִיחָא בְּתַנּוּרָא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא,
phrases.english: a piece of brick fell into her oven on a Festival,
Rabbi Chiya said to her: See,
that I want high-quality bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא נְפַל לַהּ אֲרִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ברייתא's leniency being applied.
steps.raayaObject: The leniency to clear the oven when baking is otherwise impossible.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practical conduct of רבי חייא.

steps.title: רבא's roasted duck
steps.stepSummary: רבא told his attendant to roast a duck without singeing it. This hinted that he could clear out the oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to his attendant: Roast me a duck, and be careful that it does not get singed.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story shows the same idea: setting a cooking standard that makes cleaning the oven necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oven is not cleared, the duck will get burnt. By asking for a duck that is not singed, רבא made clearing the oven 'necessary for the food,' so it was permitted.

phrases.english: Rava said to his attendant:
Roast me a duck,
and be careful not to singe it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that makes the same point as step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The leniency to clear the oven when proper cooking is otherwise impossible.

steps.title: How can רב אשי's oven be plastered?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports to רב אשי that his oven is plastered shut on יום טוב, which seems to involve kneading mud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: רב אחא from הוצל told us that they plaster the oven for the master on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a report about רב אשי's practice that looks problematic. This sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plastering usually needs mud mixed with water, which is the forbidden מלאכה of לש (kneading). So the question is how רב אשי could allow it on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Rav Acha from Hutzal told us

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר שָׁרְקִין לֵיהּ תַּנּוּרָא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא.
phrases.english: that they plaster the oven for the master on a Festival.
phrases.notes: Sealing the oven's opening keeps the heat in so the food cooks well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר לַן רַב אַחָא מֵהוּצָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related case about oven preparation, raised as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's practice of plastering his oven on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plastering requires mixing mud, which is kneading, a forbidden מלאכה.

steps.title: Ready-made mud from the bank of the פרת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that they use mud from the bank of the פרת, which is already soft, so no kneading is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We rely on the riverbank of the פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why his practice is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mud on the riverbank is already mixed and ready to use. Taking it involves no kneading, so the problem of לש disappears.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We rely on the bank of the Euphrates,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the mud was already kneaded by nature.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plastering the oven means kneading mud on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Riverbank mud is already soft, so no kneading is done.

steps.title: Only if the mud was set aside the day before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the leniency: the mud may be used only if it was designated the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only when one marked it off from the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a condition to רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mud on a riverbank is normally מוקצה, meaning not set aside for use. Marking it before יום טוב designates it for use, so it may be taken on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: set apart, not allowed to be used

phrases.english: And this applies only when one marked it off the day before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the answer of step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Riverbank mud may be used to plaster the oven only if it was designated before יום טוב.

steps.title: Plastering with ashes is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rules that plastering the oven with ashes is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: And ashes are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a final ruling: you may use ashes to seal the oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes do not bind together the way dough or mud does, so mixing them is not considered kneading. Using them to seal the oven is therefore allowed, and the earlier worry does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, preparing a new utensil is forbidden (מתקן מנא). Sweeping or clearing an oven is permitted when you cannot bake properly otherwise. You may plaster an oven with ready-made mud that was designated the day before, or with ashes.

phrases.english: Ravina said: And ashes are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another permitted material for sealing the oven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plastering the oven with ashes on יום טוב is permitted, since kneading does not apply to ashes.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: No drawing two barrels together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה forbidding drawing two barrels together to set a pot on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One may not draw two barrels together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to open a new discussion. It is setting up the next move, where אמוראים will discuss what kind of 'building' is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is placing two barrels side by side so that a pot can rest on top of both. The משנה forbids this because it looks like building. This quote is the base text that the next steps will test.

keyTerms.meaning: Draw together or set side by side (here, placing barrels close to each other)

phrases.english: And one may not draw two barrels together.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, opening a new section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of plastering the oven to a new line of the משנה about arranging barrels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing two barrels together to rest a pot on them is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב נחמן permits arranging bathroom stones
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that one may arrange the stones of a בית הכסא on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The stones of a bathroom may be set in place on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a lenient ruling. Large stones that a person sits on in an outdoor bathroom may be put into position on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting stones next to each other to sit on looks a lot like building. Even so, רב נחמן permits it. This leniency is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: To arrange them or set them in place side by side

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Stones of a lavatory,
phrases.notes: Large stones a person sits on to relieve himself.

phrases.english: It is permitted to arrange them on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a related case that seems to clash with the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arranging the stones of a בית הכסא is permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבה objects from the barrels case
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב נחמן from the משנה that forbids drawing barrels together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה challenged רב נחמן: Didn't we learn that one may not draw two barrels together to set a pot on them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב נחמן's ruling. If putting barrels together is forbidden, putting stones together should be forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases involve setting two objects side by side to make a usable structure. The משנה forbids it with barrels, so רבה argues it should also be forbidden with stones.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
To set a pot onto a stand or fire

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
One may not draw two barrels together
to set the pot on them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's permission to arrange the bathroom stones.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids setting barrels side by side, which seems to show that any arrangement that looks like building is forbidden, and that includes stones.

steps.title: The barrels are different because they form a tent
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the barrels are forbidden only because the pot on top makes an אוהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is different, because one makes a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself. The problem with the barrels is not setting them side by side. The problem is that the pot on top covers the gap between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two barrels with a pot resting across them make a covered space, like a small tent. Making an אוהל is forbidden. The bathroom stones do not make any covering, so they are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A tent; a covering over an empty space

phrases.english: He said to him: There it is different,
because he makes a tent.
phrases.notes: The pot over the gap between the barrels forms a covering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's objection by drawing a distinction between the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any arrangement that looks like building, such as barrels side by side, is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only making an אוהל is forbidden. Simply arranging stones with no covering is permitted.

steps.title: Then would building a solid bench be allowed?
steps.stepSummary: רבה זוטא asks רב אשי: by that logic, building a solid bench without a tent should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה זוטא said to רב אשי: If so, if someone built a bench on יום טוב, which does not make a tent, would that also be permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה זוטא pushes the previous answer to an extreme to show a problem with it. If only a tent is forbidden, then a solid bench should be allowed, and that sounds wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's answer suggested that 'no tent' means 'no problem.' A solid bench has no hollow space under it, so it makes no tent. Yet it is clearly real building, so the answer seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, then... (opens a challenge built from the previous logic)
A bench (here a solid one, with no space underneath)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה זוּטָא, לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabba the Younger said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בָּנָה אִצְטְבָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: But if so, if one built a bench on a Festival,
where he does not make a tent —
phrases.notes: A solid bench has no hollow underneath.

phrases.english: would it also be permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of the answer in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only making an אוהל is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'no tent' means permitted, then building a solid bench would be permitted, which is clearly not true.

steps.title: Permanent vs. temporary building, and the dignity exception
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the Torah forbids only בנין קבע. The רבנן made a גזירה against בנין עראי, but did not apply it to bathroom stones because of כבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, the Torah forbade permanent building and did not forbid temporary building. The רבנן decreed against temporary building because of permanent building. But here, because of a person's dignity, the רבנן did not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by sorting out levels of building. A bench is forbidden because of building, while the bathroom stones are an exception made for human dignity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building a bench is real building, so it is forbidden (and a permanent one is forbidden by the Torah). Temporary building is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה. For bathroom stones, the רבנן chose not to apply their גזירה so that people can relieve themselves with dignity.
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah forbids בנין קבע. The רבנן added a גזירה against בנין עראי. But they did not apply that גזירה to bathroom stones, out of respect for human dignity.
steps.confusionAlert: The stones are still a kind of temporary building. The point is not that they are 'not building.' The point is that the rabbinic גזירה was not applied to them because of dignity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that rabbinic decrees can be relaxed when human dignity is at stake. That idea, כבוד הבריות, comes up in many places in הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, בִּנְיַן קֶבַע אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: There, the Torah forbade permanent building,
the Torah did not forbid temporary building.
And the Sages decreed against temporary building
because of permanent building,
phrases.notes: So that people would not come to build permanently.

phrases.english: but here, because of his dignity,
the Sages did not decree regarding it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה זוטא by giving a new reason why the bathroom stones are permitted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explaining the reason (permanent vs. temporary building, plus a dignity exception)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason the stones are allowed is that they make no tent, so a solid bench would also be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bench is forbidden as building. The stones are temporary building, which the רבנן normally forbid, but they left them permitted because of כבוד.

steps.title: רב יהודה: Stacking a bonfire from top down vs. bottom up
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that arranging a bonfire from the top down is permitted, but from the bottom up is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This bonfire, if arranged from above to below, is permitted. If from below to above, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new rule about building-like actions. It concerns stacking wood for a fire on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stacking wood into a hollow, house-like shape from the bottom up is the normal way of building, so it is forbidden. If one holds the top pieces first and then slides the supports underneath (from the top down), it is not the normal way of building, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A bonfire or wood pile for a fire
From below to above (the normal way of building)

steps.whatToRemember: Doing a building-like action in an unusual order (top down) avoids the problem of building on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This bonfire,
phrases.notes: Wood arranged with a hollow space, like a small house.

phrases.english: from above to below — it is permitted.
from below to above — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the ordinary way of building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling about which building-like arrangements are allowed on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bonfire may be stacked from the top down, but not from the bottom up.
